name: Compromised software vendor update
summary: A trusted vendor's software update is backdoored. The organization installs it through its normal deployment tooling, giving the attacker remote access.

attack_path.description: A legitimate, signed update from the vendor contains malicious code; the vendor's access to the environment may also be abused.
The update is pushed to many hosts through the organization's own software deployment tools.
The backdoored binary keeps running and beacons to the attacker over normal web traffic; remote access tools are added.
Data is sent out over the same command-and-control channel.

key_decisions: Whether to uninstall the vendor software, accepting the loss of its function
How to coordinate with the vendor, and what to demand from them
How to scope affected hosts when the malicious code was signed and trusted
Whether contracts require notifying the organization's own customers
